Lee, Matthews, Lemieux et al. (2025) on dandiset 001195¶

Paper: Lee, Matthews, Lemieux et al., "Separable Dorsal Raphe Dopamine Projections mediate the Facets of Loneliness-like state", eLife (2025), doi:10.7554/eLife.105955. The claims file (claims/001195/10.7554-elife.105955.yaml) was written from the eLife reviewed preprint, version 2 (8 July 2025), with its Methods, legends and figure supplements.

Dataset: DANDI:001195, version 0.250408.1733 (doi:10.48324/dandi.001195/0.250408.1733). It is the only published version, and the draft has the same 230 assets and size, so it is pinned. The paper cites no version.

The dandiset holds 148 ex vivo patch-clamp cells (one NWB file each) and 41 in vivo imaging sessions of 14 mice (CNMF-E traces, footprints, the raw one-photon movie and the behaviour video as an external mp4). It holds no pose estimates, cup interactions, position or annotation of which cup holds the juvenile, and none of the behavioural, tracing or RNAscope data of Figures 1 to 5 and 8.

Claim Tested here

fig6gi-firing-responses tested
fig6j-epsp-amplitude-region tested

fig7e, fig7gh, fig7j, fig7i, fig7m, fig7-s1no, fig7-s1l, fig7-s2 (in vivo imaging) blocked: no pose, cup interactions or cup sides in the dataset; cell counts are shown in the data check
Figures 1 to 5 and 8 (17 claims: tracing, behaviour, RNAscope) blocked: not in the dataset

Loading and measures are in drn_ephys.py, which says where each parameter comes from. The notebook streams every file; it takes about 30 minutes, most of it reading the patch-clamp sweeps.

ASSETS = de.assets()
icephys = [a for a in ASSETS if a[0].endswith("_icephys.nwb")]
ophys = [a for a in ASSETS if a[0].endswith("image+ophys.nwb")]
client_assets = {a.path: a for a in de.DandiAPIClient().get_dandiset(de.DANDISET_ID, de.DANDISET_VERSION).get_assets()}
videos = {p: client_assets[p].get_content_url(follow_redirects=1, strip_query=True)
          for p in client_assets if p.endswith(".mp4")}
print(len(ASSETS), "NWB files:", len(icephys), "patch-clamp,", len(ophys), "imaging;", len(videos), "videos")

def ophys_meta(path_url):
    path, url = path_url
    with h5py.File(remfile.File(url), "r") as f:
        r = f["processing/ophys/Fluorescence/RoiResponseSeries"]
        g = f["general"]
        return {
            "path": path, "subject": g["subject/subject_id"][()].decode(),
            "subject_description": g["subject/description"][()].decode(),
            "session": f["session_description"][()].decode(),
            "n_rois": r["data"].shape[1], "n_frames": r["data"].shape[0],
            "rate_hz": float(r["starting_time"].attrs["rate"]),
            "video": f["acquisition/BehaviorVideo/external_file"][0].decode(),
            "virus": g["virus"][()].decode(), "stimulus": g["stimulus"][()].decode(),
            "experiment_description": g["experiment_description"][()].decode(),
            "processing_entries": sorted(f["processing/ophys"].keys()),
            "acquisition_entries": sorted(f["acquisition"].keys()),
        }

def video_meta(path):
    with fsspec.open(videos[path], "rb", block_size=2**20) as fh:
        c = av.open(fh)
        s = c.streams.video[0]
        return {"video": path.split("/", 1)[1], "video_s": c.duration / 1e6, "video_frames": s.frames,
                "video_fps": float(s.average_rate)}

with ThreadPoolExecutor(12) as ex:
    OPHYS = pd.DataFrame(list(ex.map(ophys_meta, ophys)))
    VID = pd.DataFrame(list(ex.map(video_meta, sorted(videos))))
OPHYS = OPHYS.merge(VID, on="video", how="left")
print("imaging metadata read")

# --- patch clamp: units and ranges of what the analysis uses
def summary(x):
    x = np.asarray(x, float)
    return f"min {np.nanmin(x):.2f}, median {np.nanmedian(x):.2f}, max {np.nanmax(x):.2f} (n={np.isfinite(x).sum()})"

# per light sweep: the holding current its description names, the current measured on ch-1 in the
# first 0.2 s, and the action potentials (0 mV crossings) in the 5 s before and the 5.5 s after the light
i0 = int(de.LIGHT_ONSET_S * de.FS)
sw = []
for c in CELLS:
    if "ChR2" not in c["virus"]:
        continue
    for kind in ("rest", "firing"):
        for s in c["sweeps"].get(kind, []):
            m = re.search(r"([+-]?\d+)\s*p[aA]", s["desc"][len(de.LIGHT_PROTOCOL):])
            sw.append({"path": c["path"], "cell": c["cell_id"], "region": c["region"], "kind": kind,
                       "described_pA": int(m.group(1)) if m else 0, "measured_pA": s["hold_pA"],
                       "spikes_before": len(de.spike_times(s["v"][i0 - 50_000:i0])),
                       "spikes_after": len(de.spike_times(s["v"][i0:i0 + 55_000]))})
SW = pd.DataFrame(sw)
ok_i = SW.measured_pA.abs() < 1e4

The files do not record when the light was on: the stimulus series of every light sweep are zero. The helper takes the first pulse 5.468 s into each 30 s light sweep, where the average response of the responding cells starts. The check below averages the rest sweeps of every ChR2 cell and compares the deflection at that time with the same measure 6 s later, after the 5.5 s response window, where no light is given.

In [6]:
def clock_check(kind="rest", opsin="ChR2"):
    rows = []
    for c in CELLS:
        if kind not in c["sweeps"] or opsin not in c["virus"]:
            continue
        avg = de.average(de.valid(c["sweeps"][kind]))
        base, resp = de.light_window(avg, de.LIGHT_ONSET_S)
        early = resp[: int(0.2 * de.FS)] - base.mean()
        base2, resp2 = de.light_window(avg, de.LIGHT_ONSET_S + 6)
        late = resp2[: int(0.2 * de.FS)] - base2.mean()
        rows.append({"true": np.abs(early).max() / base.std(), "shifted": np.abs(late).max() / base2.std()})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

def grand_onset(kind="rest", opsin="ChR2", either_sign=False):
    """Grand average of the normalized EPSPs (or responses of either sign) above 10 SD in 5.3-5.8 s, and the time it
    crosses 10% of its peak."""
    segs = []
    for c in CELLS:
        if kind in c["sweeps"] and opsin in c["virus"]:
            avg = de.average(de.valid(c["sweeps"][kind]))
            base, _ = de.light_window(avg)
            seg = avg[int(5.3 * de.FS):int(5.8 * de.FS)] - base.mean()
            if either_sign and seg.max() < -seg.min():
                seg = -seg
            if seg.max() > 10 * base.std():
                segs.append(seg / seg.max())
    if not segs:
        return 0, None, np.nan
    grand = np.mean(segs, axis=0)
    t = 5.3 + np.arange(len(grand)) / de.FS
    return len(segs), (t, grand), t[np.argmax(grand > 0.1)]

cc = clock_check()
print("max |deflection| in the first 200 ms, in baseline SDs, ChR2 rest averages (n=%d)" % len(cc))
print(" at the assumed onset: median %.1f, cells above 10 SD: %d" % (cc["true"].median(), (cc["true"] > 10).sum()))
print(" 6 s later:           median %.1f, cells above 10 SD: %d" % (cc.shifted.median(), (cc.shifted > 10).sum()))

# onset of the grand average of responding cells
from scipy.signal import find_peaks
n, (t, grand), onset = grand_onset()
print(f"grand average of {n} cells with an EPSP above 10 SD crosses 10% of its peak at {onset:.4f} s")
dg = np.gradient(np.convolve(grand, np.ones(10) / 10, mode="same"))
pk, _ = find_peaks(dg, distance=int(0.02 * de.FS), prominence=dg.max() * 0.05)
pk = t[pk][t[pk] >= onset - 0.005][:8]
print("maxima of its rate of rise from the onset on (s):", np.round(pk, 4), "; intervals (ms):", np.round(np.diff(pk) * 1e3, 1))
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 2.5))
ax.plot(t, grand); ax.axvline(de.LIGHT_ONSET_S, color="r", lw=.5)
for i in range(8): ax.axvline(de.LIGHT_ONSET_S + i / 30, color="r", lw=.3, ls=":")
ax.set_xlabel("time in sweep (s)"); ax.set_ylabel("normalized Vm"); ax.set_title("grand average, red lines: assumed pulses")
plt.show()

# --- one frame of each behaviour video, 300 s in: can the cups and the juvenile's cup be seen?
def frame_at(path, t_s=300):
    with fsspec.open(videos[path], "rb", block_size=2**20) as fh:
        c = av.open(fh)
        s = c.streams.video[0]
        c.seek(int(t_s / s.time_base), stream=s)
        for fr in c.decode(s):
            return fr.to_ndarray(format="gray")[::3, ::3]
vid_rows = OPHYS.sort_values(["group", "subject", "condition"]).reset_index(drop=True)
with ThreadPoolExecutor(12) as ex:
    frames = list(ex.map(frame_at, [p.split("/")[0] + "/" + v for p, v in zip(vid_rows.path, vid_rows.video)]))
print("frames read:", sum(f is not None for f in frames), "of", len(frames), "; frame size (pixels, every 3rd):", frames[0].shape)
fig, axs = plt.subplots(3, 14, figsize=(14, 8))
for ax in axs.flat:
    ax.axis("off")
for ax, f, (_, r) in zip(axs.flat, frames, vid_rows.iterrows()):

Checks of the description against the data:

  • Sampling at 10 kHz in every sweep used, as in the Methods.
  • In current clamp ch-1 is labelled volts, but its values are tens of pA, positive in most sweeps whose description names a positive holding current, and follow the 1 s steps from -120 to 260 pA: ch-1 is the injected current. The seal test is stored as an IZeroClampSeries but its ch-1 is a square voltage command of about 5 mV and its ch-0 a current: it is voltage clamp.
  • The descriptions and the measured current disagree in places: 77 rest sweeps in 13 cells carry more than +20 pA (up to +108 pA; B16, described as -100 pA, carries +106 pA), and 11 firing sweeps in 6 cells carry less than +5 pA (C29, described as +35 pA, carries -57 pA). 148 of the 2437 ChR2 rest sweeps, in 28 cells, fire before the light. The Methods say cells at rest were held below threshold, so those sweeps are left out of the rest averages (C51 and C52 lose all theirs).
  • 51 sweeps of one cell (P10) have a ch-1 far outside any current (beyond +-10 nA) and a membrane potential at 0 mV: they are failed sweeps and are left out. All 51 are rest sweeps; its other 28 rest sweeps (none firing before the light), its steps and its 13 firing sweeps are normal and are kept. In the first round the whole cell's rest average, with the failed sweeps in it, gave a baseline of -18 mV.
  • The files give the sex of 3 subjects (23, C137 and C150; 17 ChR2 cells) as female, where the Methods say every mouse was male. Without these cells the dataset has 25 BLP and 26 CeA cells with current steps, fewer than the paper's 27 BLP cells in the clustering; with them 31 and 30. So the cells are kept, and male mice only is shown as a variant at the end. Either the sex in the files or the paper's statement is wrong for these cells, or these cells are not among the paper's: the mice labelled male give 48 BLP cells with rest sweeps, the paper's count (fig6df).
  • Subject ids that differ only by a suffix ('4484' and '4484?', '235' and '235 cage', 'in_vivo_5' and 'in_vivo_5_2') are probably the same mice, which would make 17 subjects, not 20.
  • The light time is not in the files. The assumed onset is where the responses start, and the following maxima of the grand average fall about 33 ms apart, as 30 Hz pulses would; the response at the assumed onset is far above the same measure 6 s later. The ChrimsonR sweeps, with red, blue or both, start at the same time (grand averages cross 10% at 5.473 to 5.476 s). This is consistent with the description of 8 pulses at 30 Hz but does not prove the onset to the millisecond.
  • No text field of the files (sweep descriptions, session description, the stimulus types of the sequential recordings table, electrode descriptions) names TTX or 4-AP, so the TTX/4AP recordings of Figure 6 supplement 1D-E cannot be identified.
  • Imaging: the traces are stated at 25 Hz, but 19,211 frames at 25 Hz last 768 s while the behaviour videos last 961 s (median; one lasts 800 s); at the Methods' 20 frames/s the imaging lasts 961 s, within 4 s of the video in every session but that one. The data support 20 Hz, and the stated rate is wrong. The virus, stimulus and experiment description fields of every imaging file describe another experiment (a GRIN lens in the mPFC, Chrimson in the BLA, 589 nm light at 20 Hz), where the Methods give a lens over the CeA, Chrimson in the DRN and 620 nm light at 30 Hz.
  • The number of ROIs is about twice the paper's cell counts in every condition (above), and the files do not mark which ROIs the paper kept.
  • The behaviour videos show the arena from above with the mouse and both cups in every session; the cups are covered, so which one holds the juvenile cannot be seen in these frames.

fig6df-epsp-ipsp-at-rest¶

At the resting membrane potential, photostimulation of DRN-DAT terminals evoked both excitatory and inhibitory post-synaptic potentials in downstream cells of the BNST, CeA and BLP (19, 36 and 48 cells recorded).

Per ChR2 cell, the average of its rest sweeps (30 s light sweeps with no or negative holding current and no action potential in the 5 s before the light; Methods). Peak and trough within 0-5.5 s of the first pulse against the 5 s baseline, detected beyond 2 or 3 SD of that baseline (the criterion's readings); 5 SD is shown as a further variant. The same detection is run in a light-free window of the same average, 12 s after the light, to show how often it finds a deflection where there is no light. Cells recorded only with other protocols (20 s or 60 s sweeps, or light at 10 s) are left out because their light time cannot be fixed; their number is printed.

In [10]:
REGIONS = ["BNST", "CeA", "BLP"]
EXPECTED_REST = {"BNST": 19, "CeA": 36, "BLP": 48}
KS = (2, 3, 5)          # the criterion's readings, 2 and 3 SD, and 5 SD as a variant
rest, all_spiking = [], []
for c in CELLS:
    if "ChR2" not in c["virus"] or "rest" not in c["sweeps"]:
        continue
    sub = de.subthreshold(de.valid(c["sweeps"]["rest"]))
    if not sub:
        all_spiking.append(c["cell_id"])
        continue
    avg = de.average(sub)
    row = {"path": c["path"], "subject": c["subject"], "sex": c["sex"], "cell": c["cell_id"], "region": c["region"],
           "n_sweeps": len(sub), "n_spiking_left_out": len(c["sweeps"]["rest"]) - len(sub)}
    for k in KS:
        e = de.evoked(avg, k)
        ctl = de.evoked(avg, k, onset=de.CONTROL_ONSET_S)       # light-free window, 12 s later
        row[f"class_k{k}"], row[f"epsp_k{k}"], row[f"ipsp_k{k}"] = de.response_class(e), e["epsp"], e["ipsp"]
        row[f"ctl_class_k{k}"], row[f"ctl_epsp_k{k}"], row[f"ctl_ipsp_k{k}"] = de.response_class(ctl), ctl["epsp"], ctl["ipsp"]
    row.update({kk: e[kk] for kk in ("baseline_mV", "sd_mV", "peak_mV", "trough_mV", "area_mVs")})
    row["peak_over_sd"], row["trough_over_sd"] = e["peak_mV"] / e["sd_mV"], -e["trough_mV"] / e["sd_mV"]
    row["ctl_peak_over_sd"], row["ctl_trough_over_sd"] = ctl["peak_mV"] / ctl["sd_mV"], -ctl["trough_mV"] / ctl["sd_mV"]
    row["evoked_ap"] = de.light_window(avg)[1].max() > de.SPIKE_THRESHOLD_MV
    rest.append(row)
REST = pd.DataFrame(rest)
no_rest = cells[(cells.opsin == "ChR2") & (cells.n_rest == 0)]
print("ChR2 cells without 30 s rest sweeps (left out):", len(no_rest), dict(no_rest.region.value_counts()))
print("ChR2 cells whose every rest sweep has spikes before the light (left out):", all_spiking)
print("cells of mice labelled female (kept):", dict(REST.loc[REST.sex != "M", "region"].value_counts()))
print("cells per region:", {r: int((REST.region == r).sum()) for r in REGIONS},
      "; male mice only:", {r: int((REST[REST.sex == "M"].region == r).sum()) for r in REGIONS}, "; expected", EXPECTED_REST)

def fig6df(R, k, window=""):
    tab = pd.crosstab(R.region, R[f"{window}class_k{k}"]).reindex(REGIONS).fillna(0).astype(int)
    ok = all(R[R.region == r][f"{window}epsp_k{k}"].any() for r in REGIONS) and R[f"{window}ipsp_k{k}"].any()
    return tab, ok

for k in KS:
    tab, ok = fig6df(REST, k)
    ctab, cok = fig6df(REST, k, "ctl_")
    print(f"\nreading k={k} SD{' (variant)' if k == 5 else ''}:"); print(tab)
    print("  percent:"); print((100 * tab.div(tab.sum(axis=1), axis=0)).round(1))
    print(f"  every region has a cell with an EPSP and some cell has an IPSP: {ok}")
    print(f"  the same detection in the light-free window 12 s later (no light):"); print(ctab)
    print(f"  ... would pass there too: {cok}")

# how often the rule detects a deflection with and without light, as the threshold rises
fp = []
for k in (2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10):

               "IPSP, light %": 100 * (REST.trough_over_sd > k).mean(), "IPSP, no light %": 100 * (REST.ctl_trough_over_sd > k).mean()})
print(f"\npercent of the {len(REST)} cells with a detection, in the light window and in the light-free window:")
print(pd.DataFrame(fp).round(1).to_string(index=False))

Result: reproduced. Under both readings every region has cells with an EPSP and cells with an IPSP: at 2 SD the BNST, CeA and BLP have 15, 37 and 54 cells with an EPSP and 11, 30 and 49 with an IPSP; at 3 SD 13, 35 and 53, and 6, 14 and 38. The test alone does not show this, because the same rule passes in the light-free window too. The evidence is the contrast: at 3 SD 92.7% of cells have an EPSP and 53.2% an IPSP after the light, against 79.8% and 30.3% without light; at 5 SD 84.4% and 19.3% against 40.4% and 4.6%. The dataset holds 15, 38 and 56 ChR2 cells with usable rest sweeps where the paper reports 19, 36 and 48 (14, 35 and 48 from the mice labelled male), so the counts do not match; 19 ChR2 cells recorded only with other light protocols are left out. At 2 SD most cells are mix (73 to 84%); at 5 SD most are excitation only (62 to 74%). For IPSPs the contrast is weak at 3 SD (53.2% against 30.3%) and clear from 4 SD up (27.5% against 11.0%).

fig6gi-firing-responses¶

In cells made to fire by constant current, photostimulation increased firing in all BNST cells (5 of 5), while CeA (20 cells) and BLP (17 cells) cells showed either an increase or a decrease in firing.

Firing sweeps (set a) are the 30 s light sweeps with a positive holding current in their description (Methods). Spikes are upward crossings of 0 mV. IEI before (5 s, or 5.5 s as the Figure 6 supplement 1G variant) and 5 s after the first pulse; readings (a) mean of all IEIs pooled over sweeps, (b) mean over sweeps of each sweep's mean IEI. As a variant, set (b) adds the rest sweeps that fire before the light with a measured current above +10 pA, since the descriptions and the measured current disagree (data check).

In [11]:
EXPECTED_FIRE = {"BNST": 5, "CeA": 20, "BLP": 17}

def fire_row(c, sweeps, set_name):
    row = {"path": c["path"], "subject": c["subject"], "sex": c["sex"], "cell": c["cell_id"], "region": c["region"],
           "set": set_name, "n_sweeps": len(sweeps), "max_vm_mV": max(float(s["v"].max()) for s in sweeps),
           "spikes": sum(len(de.spike_times(s["v"])) for s in sweeps)}
    for before in (5.0, 5.5):
        r = de.iei_change(sweeps, before_s=before)
        for rd in ("a", "b"):
            row[f"{rd}_{before}_before"], row[f"{rd}_{before}_after"] = r[f"{rd}_before"], r[f"{rd}_after"]
            row[f"label_{rd}_{before}"] = de.iei_label(r[f"{rd}_before"], r[f"{rd}_after"])
    return row

fire, fire_b = [], []
for c in CELLS:
    if "ChR2" not in c["virus"]:
        continue
    if "firing" in c["sweeps"]:
        fire.append(fire_row(c, de.valid(c["sweeps"]["firing"]), "a"))
    # variant set (b): also the 'rest' sweeps that fire before the light with a measured current above +10 pA
    extra = [s for s in de.valid(c["sweeps"].get("rest", [])) if s["hold_pA"] > 10
             and len(de.spike_times(s["v"][i0 - 50_000:i0])) > 0]
    if "firing" in c["sweeps"] or extra:
        fire_b.append(fire_row(c, de.valid(c["sweeps"].get("firing", [])) + extra, "b"))
FIRE = pd.DataFrame(fire)
FIRE_B = pd.DataFrame(fire_b)

    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

Result: partially reproduced. In every reading both excitation and inhibition occur in the CeA (8 and 2) and the BLP (4 to 6 and 7 to 9), and the BNST cells that can be classed are excited (2 of 2). The third BNST cell (B7, one sweep) has no action potential (highest Vm -29 mV), so the paper's 5 of 5 cannot be checked: the dataset holds 3, 13 and 13 cells with firing sweeps where the paper reports 5, 20 and 17. Three CeA cells (C29, C39 and C47) and one BLP cell (P9) also lack an IEI before or after the light; C29 and C47 never cross 0 mV (highest Vm -59 and -49 mV), so a lower spike threshold would not change this. In set (b), 5, 17 and 17 cells, the BNST cells with an IEI are excited in three of the four readings.

fig6j-epsp-amplitude-region¶

The peak amplitude of the optically evoked EPSP differed between regions, larger in the CeA than in the BLP.

EPSP peak of the average rest trace, one value per cell with an EPSP; cells (a) excitation and mix, (b) excitation only; under each detection reading of fig6df (2 and 3 SD), with 5 SD as a variant. Kruskal-Wallis, then Dunn's test (Prism's adjustment).

In [12]:
def fig6j(k, which, R=None):
    R = REST if R is None else R
    cls = R[f"class_k{k}"]
    sel = R[cls.isin(["excitation", "mix"] if which == "a" else ["excitation"])]
    g = {r: sel[sel.region == r].peak_mV.values for r in REGIONS}
    out = {"k": k, "cells": which, **{f"n_{r}": len(g[r]) for r in REGIONS}}
    if min(len(v) for v in g.values()) < 2:
        return {**out, "H": np.nan, "p": np.nan}
    H, p = stats.kruskal(*g.values())
    dn = de.dunn(g)
    return {**out, **{f"median_{r}": np.median(g[r]) for r in REGIONS}, "H": H, "p": p,
            "dunn_CeA_BLP": dn[("CeA", "BLP")], "dunn_BNST_CeA": dn[("BNST", "CeA")], "dunn_BNST_BLP": dn[("BNST", "BLP")]}

def j_table(R=None):
    J = pd.DataFrame([fig6j(k, w, R) for k in KS for w in ("a", "b")])
    J["holds"] = (J.p < 0.05) & (J.dunn_CeA_BLP < 0.05) & (J.median_CeA > J.median_BLP)
    return J
J = j_table()
print(J.round(4).to_string())

Result: partially reproduced. The CeA median exceeds the BLP median in five of the six rows, but the test is significant in only one of the criterion's four readings: reading (a) at 3 SD, narrowly (H = 6.02, p = 0.049; Dunn CeA against BLP p = 0.043). Reading (a) at 2 SD gives p = 0.088, and reading (b) p = 0.86 and 0.27. At 2 and 3 SD most excitation cells are classed mix because the rule finds an IPSP in 67% and 30% of the light-free windows, so reading (b) keeps only 19 and 48 cells. The one passing reading rests on one cell: without C15, whose rest average carries an evoked action potential, reading (a) at 3 SD gives p = 0.075 (Dunn p = 0.071). At 5 SD, where that rate is 4.6%, both readings are significant (p = 0.016 and 0.037), and reading (a) stays so without C15 (p = 0.026). With the cells of the mice labelled male only, reading (a) is significant at 2 and 3 SD (variant at the end).

fig6k-ipsp-amplitude-region¶

The trough amplitude of the optically evoked IPSP differed between regions, deeper in the CeA than in the BLP.

IPSP trough of the average rest trace; cells (a) inhibition and mix, (b) inhibition only; detection at 2 or 3 SD, with 5 SD as a variant. One-way ANOVA, then Tukey's test and Holm-Sidak (the post hoc test is not named).

In [13]:
def fig6k(k, which, R=None):
    R = REST if R is None else R
    cls = R[f"class_k{k}"]
    sel = R[cls.isin(["inhibition", "mix"] if which == "a" else ["inhibition"])]
    g = {r: sel[sel.region == r].trough_mV.values for r in REGIONS if (sel.region == r).sum() > 0}
    out = {"k": k, "cells": which, "n_total": len(sel), **{f"n_{r}": int((sel.region == r).sum()) for r in REGIONS},
           **{f"mean_{r}": sel[sel.region == r].trough_mV.mean() for r in REGIONS}}
    usable = {r: v for r, v in g.items() if len(v) >= 2}
    if len(usable) < 2 or "CeA" not in usable or "BLP" not in usable:
        return {**out, "F": np.nan, "p": np.nan}
    F, p = stats.f_oneway(*usable.values())
    tk = pairwise_tukeyhsd(np.concatenate(list(usable.values())), np.concatenate([[r] * len(v) for r, v in usable.items()]))
    res = pd.DataFrame(tk._results_table.data[1:], columns=tk._results_table.data[0])
    t_cea_blp = float(res[((res.group1 == "BLP") & (res.group2 == "CeA")) | ((res.group1 == "CeA") & (res.group2 == "BLP"))]["p-adj"].iloc[0])
    hs = de.holm_sidak(usable)
    hs_cea_blp = hs.get(("CeA", "BLP"), hs.get(("BLP", "CeA")))
    return {**out, "groups_in_test": len(usable), "df": f"{len(usable) - 1},{sum(len(v) for v in usable.values()) - len(usable)}",
            "F": F, "p": p, "tukey_CeA_BLP": t_cea_blp, "holm_sidak_CeA_BLP": hs_cea_blp}

def k_table(R=None):
    K = pd.DataFrame([fig6k(k, w, R) for k in KS for w in ("a", "b")])
    K["holds_tukey"] = (K.p < 0.05) & (K.tukey_CeA_BLP < 0.05) & (K.mean_CeA < K.mean_BLP)
    K["holds_holm_sidak"] = (K.p < 0.05) & (K.holm_sidak_CeA_BLP < 0.05) & (K.mean_CeA < K.mean_BLP)
    K["n_within_34_pm_3.4"] = (K.n_total - 34).abs() <= 3.4
    return K
K = k_table()
print(K.round(4).to_string())
print("rows with k=5 are a variant; the criterion's readings are k=2 and 3")

paper: F(2,31) = 8.150, p = 0.0014, CeA vs BLP p = 0.0014; 34 cells

Result: partially reproduced, under the 3 SD reading. The readings disagree. At 2 SD the ANOVA on 90 cells gives p = 0.76. At 3 SD the ANOVA on 58 cells gives F(2,55) = 6.88, p = 0.0021, and CeA against BLP Tukey p = 0.0031 and Holm-Sidak p = 0.0033, with the CeA mean trough deeper (-0.78 against -0.45 mV). At 5 SD (21 cells, one BNST cell, so two groups) the CeA trough is also deeper (p < 0.0001). The 3 SD reading is adopted because it agrees with 5 SD, the threshold at which IPSPs separate from noise (19.3% of cells after the light against 4.6% without, fig6df). The false-detection rate alone does not settle it: at 3 SD the rule finds an IPSP in 30.3% of light-free windows against 53.2% after the light, so more than half of the 3 SD IPSPs may be noise, as most of the 2 SD ones are (67.0% against 82.6%). The paper's test has 34 cells; 58 is outside 34 +- 3.4. Reading (b) leaves 3 to 5 cells and cannot be tested.

fig6-s1de-monosynaptic (blocked)¶

The optically evoked EPSP and the slow component of the IPSP persisted after TTX/4AP, so the responses were typically monosynaptic.

No text field of the files names TTX or 4-AP (data check: the 103 sweep descriptions, the session descriptions, the 103 stimulus types of the sequential recordings table and the electrode descriptions; general/ has no notes, protocol, slices or pharmacology field). The sweeps recorded after TTX/4AP cannot be told from those before. Blocked, metadata_insufficient.

Baseline properties for the clustering claims¶

Per ChR2 cell from its 1 s current steps (Methods): voltage sag at -120 pA (steady state the last 100 ms, or 200 ms, of the step), ramp ratio at the largest subthreshold step (absolute Vm as written, or deflections from the pre-step Vm), firing delay at rheobase, and the maximum instantaneous frequency in the first 100 ms of the depolarizing steps (0 Hz when no two spikes fall in that time). Capacitance by the Q-method from the 5 mV seal-test pulses, the only voltage-clamp test pulses in the files (the Methods use a 5 mV, 250 ms step); no correction for the series and membrane resistance is made, so the error of this estimate depends on each cell's own resistances. Some BLP cells were also stepped from 220 pA up to 600 pA; those steps are used for rheobase.

Response label per cell (Methods): from the IEI when the cell has firing sweeps, otherwise excitation for an EPSP only, inhibition for an IPSP only, the sign of the 0-5.5 s voltage area for a mix, and none otherwise. Labels are made at 2 and 3 SD (the criterion's readings) and at 5 SD (a variant).

In [14]:
feat_rows = []
for c in CELLS:
    if "ChR2" not in c["virus"]:
        continue
    row = {"path": c["path"], "subject": c["subject"], "sex": c["sex"], "cell": c["cell_id"], "region": c["region"]}
    if "steps" in c["sweeps"]:
        for ss in (100, 200):
            f = de.step_features(c["sweeps"]["steps"], sag_ss_ms=ss) or {}
            row[f"sag_{ss}"] = f.get("sag_mV", np.nan)
        row.update({"ramp_abs": f.get("ramp_ratio", np.nan), "ramp_defl": f.get("ramp_ratio_deflection", np.nan),
                    "delay": f.get("firing_delay_ms", np.nan), "maxfreq": f.get("max_freq_hz", np.nan),
                    "step_min": f.get("min_pA", np.nan), "step_max": f.get("max_pA", np.nan)})
    if "seal" in c["sweeps"]:
        row["cap"] = de.cell_capacitance_pf(c["sweeps"]["seal"])
    feat_rows.append(row)
FEAT = pd.DataFrame(feat_rows)
FEAT = FEAT.merge(REST[["path", "peak_mV", "trough_mV", "area_mVs", *[f"{x}_k{k}" for k in KS for x in ("class", "epsp")]]],
                          on="path", how="left")
FEAT = FEAT.merge(FIRE[["path", "label_a_5.0", "label_b_5.0"]], on="path", how="left")

def label(row, k, iei):
    lab = row.get(f"label_{iei}_5.0")
    if isinstance(lab, str):
        return lab
    cls = row.get(f"class_k{k}")
    if cls == "mix":
        return "excitation" if row["area_mVs"] > 0 else "inhibition"
    return {"excitation": "excitation", "inhibition": "inhibition", "none": "none"}.get(cls, "no data")
for k in KS:
    for iei in ("a", "b"):
        FEAT[f"resp_k{k}_{iei}"] = FEAT.apply(lambda r: label(r, k, iei), axis=1)
        FEAT[f"src_k{k}_{iei}"] = np.where(FEAT[f"label_{iei}_5.0"].notna(), "IEI",
                                               np.where(FEAT[f"class_k{k}"].notna(), "rest " + FEAT[f"class_k{k}"].astype(str), "no data"))
print("ChR2 cells with current steps:", int(FEAT.step_min.notna().sum()), "; with each feature, by region:")
print(FEAT.groupby("region")[["sag_100", "ramp_abs", "delay", "maxfreq", "cap"]].count())

CEA_FEATS = ["ramp", "maxfreq", "delay", "sag"]
BLP_FEATS = ["cap", "maxfreq", "delay", "sag"]
CRIT_K = (2, 3)         # the criterion's detection readings; k=5 is a variant

def cluster(df, cols):
    X = df[cols].to_numpy(float)
    X = (X - X.min(0)) / (X.max(0) - X.min(0))
    return fcluster(linkage(X, method="ward", metric="euclidean"), 2, criterion="maxclust")

def frame_for(region, ramp, sag, feats, F=None):
    F = FEAT if F is None else F
    df = F[F.region.isin([region] if isinstance(region, str) else region)].copy()
    df["ramp"], df["sag"] = df[ramp], df[sag]
    return df.dropna(subset=feats).reset_index(drop=True)

fig6no-cea-clusters¶

Hierarchical clustering of CeA cells on four baseline properties gave two clusters, late-firing cells (cluster 1) that were excited by DRN-DAT input and regular-firing cells (cluster 2) that were mostly inhibited.

Max-min normalized ramp ratio, maximum instantaneous frequency, firing delay and sag; Ward linkage on Euclidean distance; two clusters. The cluster with the longer mean firing delay is the late-firing cluster. Every reading of the criterion is run: ramp ratio absolute or from deflections, sag steady state 100 or 200 ms, and the detection (2 or 3 SD) and IEI readings behind the labels; 5 SD labels are a variant.

In [16]:
def cea_runs(F=None):
    runs, main = [], None
    for ramp in ("ramp_abs", "ramp_defl"):
        for sag in ("sag_100", "sag_200"):
            df = frame_for("CeA", ramp, sag, CEA_FEATS, F)
            df["cl"] = cluster(df, CEA_FEATS)
            df["late"] = df.cl == df.groupby("cl").delay.mean().idxmax()
            for k in KS:
                for iei in ("a", "b"):
                    lab = df[f"resp_k{k}_{iei}"]
                    L, R = lab[df.late], lab[~df.late]
                    runs.append({"ramp": ramp, "sag": sag, "k": k, "iei": iei, "n": len(df),
                                 "n_late": len(L), "late_excited": (L == "excitation").sum(), "late_inhibited": (L == "inhibition").sum(),
                                 "late_none_or_nodata": L.isin(["none", "no data"]).sum(),
                                 "n_regular": len(R), "regular_excited": (R == "excitation").sum(),
                                 "regular_inhibited": (R == "inhibition").sum(),
                                 "regular_none_or_nodata": R.isin(["none", "no data"]).sum(),
                                 "late_all_excited": (L == "excitation").all(),
                                 "regular_over_half_inhibited": (R == "inhibition").sum() > len(R) / 2,
                                 "holds": (L == "excitation").all() and (R == "inhibition").sum() > len(R) / 2})
            if ramp == "ramp_abs" and sag == "sag_100":
                main = df.copy()
    return pd.DataFrame(runs), main

Result: not reproduced. Every reading gives two clusters of 27 cells (the paper has 26), a late-firing cluster (mean firing delay 415 against 168 ms) and a regular-firing one. The late-firing cluster is mostly excited (11 to 13 of 17 or 18 cells) but holds 2 or 3 inhibited cells (C20, a mix with a negative area, and C53, from its IEI; C41 too at 2 SD) and 3 cells without response data, so not every cell is excited as the criterion requires; 6 of the 9 or 10 regular-firing cells are inhibited, more than half. The readings agree: the first part of the criterion fails in all 16 readings at 2 and 3 SD and the second holds in all 16. With 5 SD labels the late-firing cluster has one inhibited cell (C53) and only 3 of the regular-firing cells are inhibited, so both parts fail. The criterion has no partial clause (the claims file gives one where it means one, as for fig6pq), and its first part fails in every reading. Whether the paper means every late-firing cell is asked of a reader.

def h_table(F=None):
    rows = []
    for ramp in ("ramp_abs", "ramp_defl"):
        for sag in ("sag_100", "sag_200"):
            df = frame_for("CeA", ramp, sag, CEA_FEATS, F)
            df["cl"] = cluster(df, CEA_FEATS)
            a, b = df[df.cl == 1], df[df.cl == 2]
            row = {"ramp": ramp, "sag": sag, "n1": len(a), "n2": len(b)}
            for f in CEA_FEATS:
                t, p = stats.ttest_ind(a[f], b[f])
                row[f"t_{f}"], row[f"p_{f}"] = t, p
            row["all_p<0.05"] = all(row[f"p_{f}"] < 0.05 for f in CEA_FEATS)
            rows.append(row)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

fig6pq-blp-clusters¶

BLP cells clustered into putative pyramidal neurons (cluster 1) and putative GABAergic interneurons (cluster 2); 93% of the putative pyramidal neurons were inhibited by DRN-DAT input and 62% of the putative interneurons were excited.

As for the CeA with capacitance in place of the ramp ratio. The pyramidal cluster is the one with the larger mean capacitance; whether it also has the lower maximum frequency is printed. Percentages over all cells of a cluster.

In [18]:
def blp_runs(F=None):
    runs, main = [], None
    for sag in ("sag_100", "sag_200"):
        df = frame_for("BLP", "ramp_abs", sag, BLP_FEATS, F)
        df["cl"] = cluster(df, BLP_FEATS)
        means = df.groupby("cl")[["cap", "maxfreq"]].mean()
        pyr = means.cap.idxmax()
        df["pyr"] = df.cl == pyr
        for k in KS:
            for iei in ("a", "b"):
                lab = df[f"resp_k{k}_{iei}"]
                P, I = lab[df.pyr], lab[~df.pyr]
                pi, ie = 100 * (P == "inhibition").mean(), 100 * (I == "excitation").mean()
                runs.append({"sag": sag, "k": k, "iei": iei, "n": len(df), "n_pyr": len(P), "n_int": len(I),
                             "pyr_has_lower_maxfreq": means.maxfreq[pyr] < means.maxfreq.drop(pyr).iloc[0],
                             "pyr_inhibited_%": pi, "pyr_excited_%": 100 * (P == "excitation").mean(),
                             "int_excited_%": ie, "int_inhibited_%": 100 * (I == "inhibition").mean(),
                             "within_tol": abs(pi - 93) <= 9.3 and abs(ie - 62) <= 6.2,
                             "direction": (P == "inhibition").mean() > 0.5 and (I == "excitation").mean() > 0.5})
        if sag == "sag_100":
            main = df.copy()
    return pd.DataFrame(runs), main

fig6-s1jk-cluster-voltage-area¶

The total voltage area evoked by DRN-DAT stimulation differed between the two clusters in both the CeA and the BLP, and the EPSP peak amplitude differed between the BLP clusters but not between the CeA clusters.

Total voltage area 0-5.5 s against the 5 s baseline of the average rest trace (Methods); Mann-Whitney U for the area, unpaired t-test for the EPSP peak of cells with an EPSP, between the clusters of each clustering reading.

In [20]:
def jk(df, grp, region, reading):
    out = {"region": region, "reading": reading}
    a, b = df[df[grp]], df[~df[grp]]
    aa, bb = a.area_mVs.dropna(), b.area_mVs.dropna()
    out["n_area"] = f"{len(aa)}+{len(bb)}"
    out["U"], out["p_area"] = stats.mannwhitneyu(aa, bb, alternative="two-sided") if len(aa) and len(bb) else (np.nan, np.nan)
    out["median_area_1"], out["median_area_2"] = aa.median(), bb.median()
    for k in KS:
        ea = a[a[f"epsp_k{k}"] == True].peak_mV
        eb = b[b[f"epsp_k{k}"] == True].peak_mV
        t, p = stats.ttest_ind(ea, eb) if len(ea) > 1 and len(eb) > 1 else (np.nan, np.nan)
        out[f"n_epsp_k{k}"], out[f"t_epsp_k{k}"], out[f"p_epsp_k{k}"] = f"{len(ea)}+{len(eb)}", t, p
    return out

def jk_table(F=None):
    rows = []
    for ramp in ("ramp_abs", "ramp_defl"):
        for sag in ("sag_100", "sag_200"):
            df = frame_for("CeA", ramp, sag, CEA_FEATS, F)
            df["cl"] = cluster(df, CEA_FEATS)
            df["g"] = df.cl == df.groupby("cl").delay.mean().idxmax()
            rows.append(jk(df, "g", "CeA (late vs regular)", f"{ramp}, {sag}"))
    for sag in ("sag_100", "sag_200"):
        df = frame_for("BLP", "ramp_abs", sag, BLP_FEATS, F)
        df["cl"] = cluster(df, BLP_FEATS)
        df["g"] = df.cl == df.groupby("cl").cap.mean().idxmax()
        rows.append(jk(df, "g", "BLP (pyramidal vs interneuron)", sag))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

def jk_holds(JK, k):
    cea, blp = JK[JK.region.str.startswith("CeA")], JK[JK.region.str.startswith("BLP")]
    return bool((cea.p_area < 0.05).all() and (blp.p_area < 0.05).all() and (blp[f"p_epsp_k{k}"] < 0.05).all() and (cea[f"p_epsp_k{k}"] >= 0.05).all())
JK = jk_table()
print(JK.round(4).to_string())
for k in KS:
    print(f"k={k}{' (variant)' if k == 5 else ''}: holds in every reading:", jk_holds(JK, k))

Result: reproduced, with the cells of the mice labelled female. Under every reading the total voltage area differs between the CeA clusters (Mann-Whitney U = 97 or 101, p = 0.0001 or below) and between the BLP clusters (U = 38, p = 0.020), the EPSP peak differs between the BLP clusters (t-test p = 0.023 at 2 and 3 SD) and not between the CeA clusters (p = 0.097 to 0.21). With the mice labelled male only the BLP tests fail (area p = 0.11, EPSP peak p = 0.099) while the CeA tests still hold (variant at the end), so the outcome rests on keeping the cells labelled female.

fig6-s1ln-combined-clusters¶

Clustering CeA and BLP cells together gave two clusters with a response pattern very similar to that of the separate clusterings.

Five features (ramp ratio, capacitance, maximum frequency, firing delay, sag), max-min normalized, Ward, two clusters, on the CeA and BLP cells with all five. The criterion asks that the excited cluster be the same in both regions. Figure 6 supplement 1N, as drawn, shows the CeA cells of cluster 1 mostly excited and its BLP cells inhibited, and the reverse in cluster 2; that pattern is checked as a variant (figure_s1n_pattern), and whether the criterion misreads the figure is asked of a reader (questions/001195.yaml).

In [21]:
FIVE = ["ramp", "cap", "maxfreq", "delay", "sag"]
from scipy.cluster.hierarchy import dendrogram

def ln_table(F=None):
    rows, comb = [], None
    for ramp in ("ramp_abs", "ramp_defl"):
        for sag in ("sag_100", "sag_200"):
            df = frame_for(["CeA", "BLP"], ramp, sag, FIVE, F)
            df["cl"] = cluster(df, FIVE)
            for k in KS:
                for iei in ("a", "b"):
                    lab = df[f"resp_k{k}_{iei}"]
                    row = {"ramp": ramp, "sag": sag, "k": k, "iei": iei, "n": len(df)}
                    exc_cluster = {}
                    for reg in ("CeA", "BLP"):
                        for cl in (1, 2):
                            s = lab[(df.region == reg) & (df.cl == cl)]
                            row[f"{reg}_c{cl}"] = f"{(s == 'excitation').sum()}e/{(s == 'inhibition').sum()}i/{len(s)}"
                            row[f"{reg}_c{cl}_exc_frac"] = (s == "excitation").mean() if len(s) else np.nan
                            row[f"{reg}_c{cl}_inh_frac"] = (s == "inhibition").mean() if len(s) else np.nan
                        e = [cl for cl in (1, 2) if row[f"{reg}_c{cl}_exc_frac"] > 0.5]
                        i = [cl for cl in (1, 2) if row[f"{reg}_c{cl}_inh_frac"] > 0.5]
                        exc_cluster[reg] = e[0] if len(e) == 1 and len(i) == 1 and e != i else None
                    split = exc_cluster["CeA"] is not None and exc_cluster["BLP"] is not None
                    # the criterion: the excited cluster the same in both regions
                    row["holds"] = split and exc_cluster["CeA"] == exc_cluster["BLP"]
                    # Figure 6-S1N as drawn: CeA excited and BLP inhibited in one cluster, the reverse in the other
                    row["figure_s1n_pattern"] = split and exc_cluster["CeA"] != exc_cluster["BLP"]
                    rows.append(row)
            if ramp == "ramp_abs" and sag == "sag_100":
                comb = df.copy()
    return pd.DataFrame(rows), comb

Result: not reproduced. In every reading the combined clustering puts the CeA late-firing cells with the BLP putative pyramidal cells (cluster 2) and the CeA regular-firing cells with the BLP putative interneurons (cluster 1); the combined clusters agree with the separate ones in 51 of 52 cells. The CeA cells of cluster 2 are mostly excited (11 to 13 of 17 or 19) and 5 or 6 of the 8 or 10 CeA cells of cluster 1 are inhibited, while the BLP cells of cluster 1 are mostly excited (6 of 8) and those of cluster 2 mostly inhibited (10 or 11 of 17): the excited cluster is not the same in the two regions, as the criterion requires. This is the pattern Figure 6 supplement 1N draws, and the variant that checks it holds in every reading at 2 and 3 SD (not at 5 SD, where 9 of the 17 BLP cells of cluster 2 are excited).

fig7-s1ef-red-vs-blue¶

Ex vivo, red light evoked ChrimsonR-mediated potentials in CeA cells with much larger peak amplitude and area than the blue light (0.3 or 0.2 mW) used for imaging.

The ChrimsonR cells' sweeps are named by description: "635nm ... every 30s" (red alone), "..., +0.3mW blue light" and "..., +0.2mW blue light" (read as the blue light conditions of Figure 7 supplement 1E-F), and "..., +0.3mW cont blue light" (red during constant blue, panels G-I). The blue descriptions begin with the red protocol and do not say whether the blue sweeps also carried red pulses; reading them as blue alone is an assumption, supported by their small responses and by their onset, the same as that of the red sweeps (data check). Amplitude readings: (a) the largest absolute deflection from the 5 s baseline, (b) the EPSP peak, or the IPSP trough magnitude when only an IPSP is detected (2 or 3 SD). Area readings: the magnitude of the signed 0-5.5 s area, and the area of the absolute deflection. Repeated measures one-way ANOVA across the three lights on the cells with all three.

In [22]:
def psp(avg, k):
    e = de.evoked(avg, k)
    a_abs = max(e["peak_mV"], -e["trough_mV"])
    if e["epsp"]:
        a_b = e["peak_mV"]
    elif e["ipsp"]:
        a_b = -e["trough_mV"]
    else:
        a_b = 0.0
    return {"amp_a": a_abs, f"amp_b_k{k}": a_b, "area_signed": abs(e["area_mVs"]), "area_abs": e["abs_area_mVs"],
            f"detected_k{k}": e["epsp"] or e["ipsp"]}
crow = []
for c in CELLS:
    if "Chrimson" not in c["virus"]:
        continue
    for cond in ("red", "blue03", "blue02", "red_contblue"):
        if cond in c["sweeps"]:
            avg = de.average(c["sweeps"][cond])
            r = {"path": c["path"], "subject": c["subject"], "sex": c["sex"], "cell": c["cell_id"], "cond": cond,
                 "n_sweeps": len(c["sweeps"][cond])}
            for k in KS:
                r.update(psp(avg, k))
            crow.append(r)
CHR = pd.DataFrame(crow)
print("ChrimsonR cells per condition:", CHR.groupby("cond").path.nunique().to_dict(),
      "; cells of mice labelled female (kept):", CHR[CHR.sex != "M"].groupby("cond").cell.unique().map(list).to_dict())

def ef_table(CH):
    three = CH[CH.cond.isin(["red", "blue03", "blue02"])]
    complete = three.groupby("path").cond.nunique()
    T3 = three[three.path.isin(complete[complete == 3].index)]
    EF = []
    for m in ["amp_a", "amp_b_k2", "amp_b_k3", "area_signed", "area_abs"]:
        res = AnovaRM(T3, depvar=m, subject="path", within=["cond"]).fit().anova_table
        w = T3.pivot(index="path", columns="cond", values=m)
        EF.append({"measure": m, "F": res["F Value"].iloc[0], "df": f"{res['Num DF'].iloc[0]:.0f},{res['Den DF'].iloc[0]:.0f}",
                   "p": res["Pr > F"].iloc[0], **{f"mean_{c}": w[c].mean() for c in ("red", "blue03", "blue02")},
                   "red>0.3mW": int((w.red > w.blue03).sum()), "red>0.2mW": int((w.red > w.blue02).sum()), "n": len(w),
                   "p_red_vs_0.3 (paired t)": stats.ttest_rel(w.red, w.blue03).pvalue,
                   "p_red_vs_0.2 (paired t)": stats.ttest_rel(w.red, w.blue02).pvalue})
    EF = pd.DataFrame(EF)
    EF["holds"] = (EF.p < 0.05) & (EF["red>0.3mW"] > EF.n / 2) & (EF["red>0.2mW"] > EF.n / 2)
    return EF, T3
EF, T3 = ef_table(CHR)
print("cells with all three lights:", T3.path.nunique(), "(paper: 9, from F(2,16))")
print(EF.round(4).to_string())
print("\nper cell (amplitude reading a, mV):")
print(T3.pivot(index=["subject", "cell"], columns="cond", values="amp_a").round(2))

Result: reproduced, reading the blue sweeps as blue light alone. In the 9 ChrimsonR cells with all three lights (the paper's 9), red light evokes larger potentials than either blue light under every reading: amplitude F(2,16) = 25.6, p < 0.0001 (mean 9.9 mV against 1.8 and 0.9 mV), larger in 8 of 9 cells against each blue; area F(2,16) = 11.0 or 7.0, p = 0.001 or 0.0067, larger in 9 of 9. The paper's F values (200.1 and 404.2) are much larger; one cell (C1, 0.68 mV to red) barely responds. The per-cell values support reading the blue sweeps as blue light alone: in C4 and C9 of subject 235, red light during constant blue gives 16.1 and 11.9 mV (fig7-s1hi), while the blue sweeps give 1.14 mV or less, so those sweeps cannot be red pulses under blue light.

def hi_table(CH):
    two = CH[CH.cond.isin(["red", "red_contblue"])]
    both = two.groupby("path").cond.nunique()
    T2 = two[two.path.isin(both[both == 2].index)]
    HI = []
    for m in ["amp_a", "amp_b_k2", "amp_b_k3", "area_signed", "area_abs"]:
        w = T2.pivot(index="path", columns="cond", values=m)
        t, p = stats.ttest_rel(w.red, w.red_contblue)
        HI.append({"measure": m, "t": t, "df": len(w) - 1, "p": p, "mean_red": w.red.mean(), "mean_red_during_blue": w.red_contblue.mean(),
                   "smaller_during_blue": int((w.red_contblue < w.red).sum()), "n": len(w)})
    HI = pd.DataFrame(HI)
    HI["holds"] = (HI.p < 0.05) & (HI.mean_red_during_blue < HI.mean_red)
    return HI, T2

Result: partially reproduced. A PSP is detected during constant blue light in all 13 cells at 2 and 3 SD (10 of 13 at 5 SD). The amplitude is smaller during blue light (mean 4.1 against 8.1 mV, paired t(12) = 3.23, p = 0.0072, smaller in 11 of 13; reading b p = 0.0083, 10 of 13), but the area is not significantly smaller (p = 0.26 and 0.16, smaller in 12 and 11 of 13). The paper finds both smaller. Detection in 13 of 13 at 2 and 3 SD says little, since the rule detects deflections in many light-free windows (fig6df); at 5 SD it is 10 of 13.

In vivo imaging claims (blocked)¶

fig7e, fig7gh, fig7j, fig7i, fig7m, fig7-s1no, fig7-s1l and fig7-s2 all need, per session, when the mouse interacted with the social and the object cup, or its time on each side (Methods: SLEAP pose with 15 keypoints, the nose within 1.3 cup diameters and the cup in a 90 degree cone). The imaging files hold the CNMF-E traces and footprints, the raw movie and a link to the behaviour video, and nothing else: no pose, no interaction or position series, no epochs for the habituation and test periods, and no record of which cup held the juvenile. The SLEAP model is not published. The behaviour videos (data check) show the mouse and both cups from above, so side times could in principle be tracked from them, but the cups are covered and nothing in the files says which held the juvenile; tracking was not attempted. The footprints would allow the co-registration behind fig7i's 202 cells, but its finding is the overlap of social-excited cells, which needs the interactions; it was not run. The data check above shows what is there, and how the ROI counts compare with the paper's cell counts.

Variant: male mice only¶

The Methods use male mice only, and the files label the subjects of 17 ChR2 cells (subjects 23, C137 and C150) female. The analysis above keeps them, because without them the dataset has fewer cells with current steps than the paper clusters (data check). Here every tested claim is rerun on the cells of the mice labelled male, so that the effect of that choice can be seen.

With the cells of the mice labelled male only, the outcomes of fig6df, fig6gi, fig6-s1h, fig6-s1i, fig7-s1ef and fig7-s1hi do not change. fig6j holds in reading (a) at 2 and 3 SD (p = 0.022 and 0.014), and fig6k at 3 SD (p = 0.0052). The clustering claims lose cells (23 CeA and 22 BLP, against the paper's 26 and 27): fig6no still fails. fig6-s1jk no longer holds: the BLP area (p = 0.11) and BLP EPSP peak (p = 0.099) tests are not significant, while the CeA area test is (p = 0.0047 or below) and the CeA EPSP test is not (p = 0.076 to 0.32), as the criterion asks. fig6pq keeps its direction at 2 and 3 SD (56 to 63% of the pyramidal cluster inhibited, 83% of the other excited) and loses it at 5 SD (44%). In the combined clustering the criterion holds in no reading, and the pattern of Figure 6 supplement 1N holds in 6 of 8 readings at 2 SD, 4 of 8 at 3 SD and none at 5 SD. It fails mostly in the readings with the ramp ratio from deflections, where the male-only clustering splits the cells differently and CeA cluster 2 is not clearly inhibited (4 to 6 excited and 6 to 8 inhibited of 14).

Summary¶

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

Claim Outcome
fig6df-epsp-ipsp-at-rest reproduced (cell counts differ: 15, 38, 56 against 19, 36, 48)
fig6gi-firing-responses partially reproduced (3, 13, 13 firing cells against 5, 20, 17; one BNST cell cannot be classed)
fig6j-epsp-amplitude-region partially reproduced (significant in one of the criterion's four readings, and at 5 SD)
fig6k-ipsp-amplitude-region partially reproduced under the adopted 3 SD reading (58 cells against 34)
fig6-s1de-monosynaptic blocked: TTX/4AP sweeps not marked
fig6no-cea-clusters not reproduced (2 or 3 inhibited cells in the late-firing cluster; asked of a reader)

In vivo imaging (8 claims) blocked: no pose, interactions or cup sides
Figures 1 to 5 and 8 (17 claims) blocked: data not in the dataset

How the analysis differs from the paper's:

  • The light time is not in the files; the first pulse is taken 5.468 s into each 30 s light sweep, where the responses start. Cells recorded only with other light protocols (20 s and 60 s sweeps, light at other times) are left out, and the counts of cells at rest and firing differ from the paper's.
  • Rest sweeps that fire before the light are left out of the rest averages, as the Methods hold cells at rest below threshold, and 51 failed sweeps of one cell are left out.
  • The paper's EPSP and IPSP were measured by hand in Clampfit with no stated threshold; here a deflection is detected beyond 2 or 3 SD of the 5 s baseline of the average trace, the criterion's readings. In a light-free window of the same traces this rule finds an EPSP in 94% and 80% of cells and an IPSP in 67% and 30%, so it finds more IPSPs than the paper reports; 5 SD (40% and 5%) is shown as a variant.
  • The cells of the three subjects the files label female are kept, although the Methods use male mice; male mice only is shown as a variant.
  • Capacitance is taken from the 5 mV seal-test pulses by the Q-method, not from the paper's 250 ms step and MATLAB code, which are not in the files or published.
  • The ChrimsonR sweeps are matched to the light conditions by their descriptions.

What was found about the dataset:

  • The light timing is not recorded; the stimulus series of the light sweeps are zero, and the protocol is given only in free text. The holding current the descriptions give disagrees with the measured current in 88 sweeps.
  • In current clamp the injected current (ch-1) is labelled volts; the seal test is stored as an IZeroClampSeries but is voltage clamp. 51 sweeps of one cell (P10) are empty (0 mV) with a ch-1 outside any plausible current.
  • No sweep or file is marked as recorded in TTX/4AP.
  • Two cells named P (the BLP naming) are labelled BNST.
  • Three subjects (17 ChR2 cells) are labelled female where the paper used male mice only, and some subject ids differ only by a suffix. Either the label or the paper is wrong, or these cells are not among the paper's.
  • The imaging traces are stated at 25 Hz, but their length matches the behaviour video only at 20 Hz, the Methods' rate. The imaging files' virus, stimulus and experiment descriptions describe another experiment (GRIN lens in the mPFC, Chrimson in the BLA, 589 nm light at 20 Hz for 5 min).
  • The imaging files hold about twice as many ROIs as the paper's cell counts (869, 913 and 854 against 429, 441 and 484 for the ChrimsonR mice), with nothing marking the ROIs the paper kept, and no pose, interaction or cup-side data, so none of the in vivo findings can be tested.
